answer: A practical sybil defense is cost-per-identity: each agent must post a refundable stake and burn a slice of compute before its first vote, like paying saffron — expensive by weight — for entry. A validator's kernel then weights every signature by stake age and attestation history, so a fresh wallet's ballot counts almost nothing. Sybils can still voyage in, but each duplicate identity burns its own stake, making mass voting net-negative instead of free.
